title: User Schema Definition
description: Master schema for a user type definition. Administrators author one of these per user type (e.g. human, service-account). The flow engine and policy engine consume the field annotations to build capability payloads and narrow authentication requirements. This schema does NOT describe a user record — it describes the shape and annotations of user records of a given type.

slug.description: Stable identifier for this user type. Referenced by flow definitions via config.schema_slug. Must be unique within the project.

name.description: Human-readable display name for this user type.

user_schema.description: The JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) that describes the shape of a user record of this type, extended with x-* annotations consumed by the flow and policy engines.

title.description: Human-readable name for this user type (mirrors top-level name, used in JSON Schema tooling).

description.description: Optional description of this user type.

required.description: Field names that must be present when creating a user of this type.

properties.description: Field definitions for this user type, keyed by field name. Each field may carry x-* annotations consumed by the flow and policy engines.

x-auth-methods.description: Which authentication methods are available for this user type. The policy engine uses this to narrow what factors it can require. If absent, all methods are treated as disabled.

user_field.description: A top-level field in a user record schema. May be a scalar, an object with one level of nested leaf fields, or an array of leaf items. Nesting is intentionally capped at one level — the flow engine flattens object properties into dot-notation fields (e.g. address.street) and deeper nesting is not supported by the engine.

type.description: JSON Schema primitive type of this field.

format.description: JSON Schema format hint (e.g. email, uri, date). The flow engine maps this to the HTML input type sent to the frontend.

title.description: Human-readable label for this field. The flow engine uses this as the default field label when no i18n override is configured.

description.description: Optional field description for admin tooling.

enum.description: Restricts the field to a fixed set of values.

minLength.description: Minimum string length. Forwarded to the flow engine's field validation object.

maxLength.description: Maximum string length. Forwarded to the flow engine's field validation object.

pattern.description: Regex pattern the value must match. Forwarded to the flow engine's field validation object.

properties.description: Nested scalar fields for object-typed properties (e.g. address.street, address.city). Values must be leaf fields — further nesting is not permitted because the flow engine only flattens one level deep.

items.description: Item schema for array-typed fields. Must be a leaf field — nested objects inside arrays are not supported by the flow engine.

x-identifier.description: When true, this field is used to resolve the user during the identifier step (maps to OIDC login_hint). At most one field per schema should be marked x-identifier.

x-verify.description: After the flow engine collects this field, it automatically injects a verification step (OTP code sent to the collected value). Only valid on string fields that hold a contact address.

x-mfa.description: Marks this field as an MFA delivery channel. The policy engine reads this to determine which OTP factors are available for this user type.

x-sensitive.description: When true, the field value is redacted from audit events and logs. Use for passwords, tokens, and PII that should not appear in traces.

x-editable.description: When true, the field appears in profiling and self-service flows, allowing the user to update it post-registration. Fields without x-editable (or with x-editable: false) are read-only after creation.

x-unique.description: Uniqueness scope. The flow engine validates this constraint on form submit before persisting. instance = unique across the whole Zitadel instance; org = unique within the user's organization.

x-claim.description: Maps this field to an OIDC/SAML claim path for auto-population during SSO login. Uses dot notation (e.g. claims.email, claims.given_name).

scalar_field.description: A scalar field nested inside an object or array field. Cannot itself contain properties or items — the flow engine does not support more than one level of nesting. Carries the same scalar constraints as user_field but omits properties, items, and x-* annotations (annotations are only meaningful on top-level fields).

type.description: Scalar type only — object and array are not permitted at leaf depth.

auth_methods.description: Declares which authentication methods are available for users of this type. The policy engine uses this to narrow the set of factors it can require — a method disabled here can never be required by policy.

enabled.description: Whether this method is available for users of this type.

position.description: Display order hint for credential step rendering. Lower = shown first.

schema.title: Human User
schema.description: Standard interactive user with email/password and passkey support.

schema.title: Service Account
schema.description: Non-interactive machine user. Only API key authentication is allowed — no passwords, passkeys, or SSO.
